title: Redbridge Financial - Implementation Kickoff & Security Brief
summary: Kickoff for Redbridge Financial's Redwood implementation. Covered deployment modes (VPC/private vs hosted), security requirements (SAML, KMS, audit logs, SOC2), basic network topologies, pilot scope (chat and embeddings for customer support automation), and initial perf/scale benchmarks. Action items assigned for network prep, test dataset for quality checks, and timeline for pilot go-live.
topics: Security & compliance checklist (KMS, SSO, audit logs)
action_items: Marco Silva - Run 3-model perf benchmark with 1k/5k token scenarios and share results - due 2026-08-31
Noah Greene - Provide network CIDR and proxy/firewall rules for VPC peering - due 2026-08-27
Marta Ruiz - Confirm internal stakeholder list and roles for pilot (security, infra, product) - due 2026-08-26
Priya Desai - Draft pilot success criteria doc and invite to review - due 2026-08-28
next_steps: Redwood to send VPC deployment checklist and security package (SOC2 summary, encryption docs)
Schedule SE-led benchmark session week of 8/31
Customer to upload a redacted sample of support transcripts for evals
Follow-up meeting for pilot kickoff on 2026-09-02 (tentative)
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-08-24
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Aisha, Marco, Priya (Redwood); Jared, Marta, Noah, Hannah (Redbridge)

[00:00] Aisha Khan: hey everyone thanks for making time today uh quick roll call before we jump in
[00:08] Jared Bloom: here, thanks aisha, uh excited to get this started
[00:11] Marta Ruiz: Marta here, good afternoon
[00:14] Marco Silva: Marco here from solutions eng
[00:16] Noah Greene: Noah here, I'll be covering security stuff
[00:19] Priya Desai: Priya from CS hi all
[00:24] Aisha Khan: great, objective for the call is to align on implementation approach, security handshake, and pilot scope. we'll call out immediate blockers and owners

Summary / Intro
[00:40] Aisha Khan: quick background — redwood offers hosted, dedicated, and private vpc deployments, most customers start hosted but given your regulator constraints we expect to look at private vpc or dedicated nodes, yes?
[00:56] Marta Ruiz: yeah our preference is private VPC with customer managed keys, we need to keep logs in our splunk cluster and we have SSO requirements. also data residency within east-usa region is preferred
[01:12] Hannah Lee: and product wants a pilot for support automation — embeddings for search + chat for triage, low latency is important but cost matters too

Deployment options & network
[01:36] Marco Silva: so for private we'll ship a lightweight control-plane integration but runtime sits in your VPC or peered account; for Dedicated there's reserved capacity on Redwood's hardware. tradeoffs: dedicated gives predictable throughput but private vpc gives more control over networking and keys
[01:58] Noah Greene: two immediate asks — one, KMS/HSM integration for encryption at rest, two, audit log delivery to our SIEM. we prefer bring-your-own-keys (BYOK) so master key never leaves our KMS
[02:16] Marco Silva: yep we support KMS integrations and HSM workflows — sometimes the name of the product shows up as "Red wood private" in some docs, that's just transcribe noise but capability is full BYOK. audit logs can be streamed over syslog or S3 with lifecycle rules
[02:36] Marta Ruiz: for network we need a list of ports and CIDRs, and do you support egress through our proxy?
[02:45] Marco Silva: yes, we can route egress through customer proxies, we will put together firewall rules. expect a small set of endpoints for control plane and model pulls

Security & Compliance details
[03:05] Noah Greene: SOC 2 is table stakes. do you have SOC 2 type II? also need penetration testing reports and certs
[03:12] Aisha Khan: Redwood has SOC 2 type II and ISO summary available; we'll share the security pack after the call. we also have an internal team that can sign an NDA or specific data processing agreement if needed
[03:28] Noah Greene: SSO - we use SAML and SCIM for provisioning, will you integrate with our IDP?
[03:34] Priya Desai: we support SAML and user provisioning via SCIM, role-based access control (RBAC) will map to your groups; we'll include an example metadata file in the security package
[03:44] Jared Bloom: auditability — we need token-level cost traces and request IDs mapped into our logs
[03:51] Marco Silva: request IDs are included in every response header and we can ship usage events to a customer side collector. token-level cost breakdown is in Console by route, and we can export those metrics
[04:04] Marta Ruiz: data residency note again — east-usa region, can you confirm availability?
[04:09] Aisha Khan: yes east-usa region is available for private infra; we'll confirm specific AZs in the post-call doc

Pilot scope and success criteria
[04:28] Hannah Lee: product's goal is reduce average handle time on support tickets by 20% using embeddings search and a chat suggestion layer. timeline is 6 weeks for pilot to validate viability with a 1-week baseline collection period
[04:44] Priya Desai: we'll workshop success criteria and measurement, but initial hypothesis: decrease time to first meaningful reply, increase deflection rate for FAQs, and quality threshold of >0.75 for retrieval precision on a holdout set
[04:58] Jared Bloom: acceptance criteria must include security sign-off, and a perf SLO of p95 under 350ms for the chat path in the pilot environment
[05:11] Marco Silva: that p95 target depends heavily on batching and KV cache warmup — for 350ms we'll likely choose the quantized LLM variant and enable prefix caching, we'll demonstrate in the benchmark run

Benchmarking & cost conversation
[05:34] Marco Silva: Action wise I'll run benchmarks across three model variants and two sequence lengths (1k, 5k). we'll measure p50/p95, tokens/sec, and cost-per-1k tokens to give you unit economics
[05:46] Marta Ruiz: also include a failover policy — if cloud capacity is constrained can you fallback to a smaller model automatically? we need graceful degradation
[05:55] Marco Silva: yes automated fallback to compatible model variants is supported, and we can set routing policies by latency vs cost
[06:04] Jared Bloom: competitors we've evaluated — Anthropic's Claude for chat, and OpenAI. leaning to open models if costs look better, but RD wants more control

Integration touchpoints
[06:22] Priya Desai: integration points: ingest pipeline for transcripts (S3 or streaming), Console setup for team access, RBAC groups, webhook endpoints for suggested responses, and metric export to your datadog or splunk
[06:34] Marta Ruiz: we will prefer S3 for batch uploads and a Kafka stream for near real time. can you consume Kafka or provide a connector?
[06:42] Marco Silva: we don't consume Kafka directly out of the box, but we can provide a lightweight connector lambda or a S3 sink pattern; we'll note a few patterns in the implementation guide

Questions from the customer
[07:01] Hannah Lee: will the redwood console show prompt-level diffs for evals? product wants to track prompt regressions across model rollouts
[07:09] Marco Silva: yes, Console has an evals dashboard and you can pin prompt sets and see regression alerts. transcription sometimes shows it as "roll out diffs" but the feature's there
[07:19] Noah Greene: how long are KV caches persisted? if a node restarts is the cache lost?
[07:25] Marco Silva: KV caches are in-memory per node by default; for longer-lived caches we support a distributed cache layer, but there's tradeoffs in complexity. for the pilot in private VPC we can enable a shared cache option to warm across nodes

Operational runbook items
[07:43] Aisha Khan: Priya will be your CS lead — weekly check-ins during pilot, escalation path to Marco for SE triage, and an on-call for production later. we'll provide a basic runbook and incident playbooks
[07:55] Priya Desai: onboarding cadence: week 0 baseline data ingest, week 1-2 model evaluation, week 3 perf tuning, week 4 pilot validation and metrics review, week 5 go/no-go decision

Network specifics (customer provides details)
[08:12] Noah Greene: i'll get you a list of egress proxies and required CIDR blocks; we need explicit hostnames for the control plane so we can add to allowlist
[08:20] Marco Silva: we'll include fully qualified domain names and a minimal port set in the checklist, plus TLS fingerprints if needed

Pricing and procurement notes
[08:34] Jared Bloom: procurement question — what does the committed monthly for dedicated look like versus pure usage? we might start with private hosted usage and then move to reserved capacity if adoption is high
[08:45] Aisha Khan: we can send a pricing matrix post-call with hosted per-token and dedicated reserved options. for pilot we'd recommend usage mode to avoid upfront commit until we hit scale

Minor transcription noise / clarifications
[09:02] Marco Silva: sometimes the transcripter spells model names weirdly — for example "quantized llama" got output as "Quantered llama" in an earlier doc, ignore that

Wrap and recap
[09:18] Aisha Khan: recap — action items: Marco runs benchmarks, Noah sends network details, Marta confirms stakeholders, Priya drafts success criteria. Redwood will share a security package (SOC 2 summary, pen test summary), deployment checklist, and an initial runbook. We'll tentatively meet first week of september to kick the pilot.
[09:44] Jared Bloom: sounds good, thank you. quick Q — can you include an example SAML metadata file in the package?
[09:50] Priya Desai: yes we'll include SAML metadata + SCIM mapping example
[09:54] Hannah Lee: please include an example of the event payload for suggested replies so our engineering can wire it up
[09:59] Marco Silva: will do — event schema and webhook examples included

Closing
[10:12] Aisha Khan: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and the package. expect docs in your inbox within 24 hours.
[10:18] Marta Ruiz: thanks all
[10:20] Jared Bloom: appreciate it, bye
[10:22] Priya Desai: bye everyone

End of recording
